title: Console: customizable cost-suggestions cards with diffs and immutable apply audit trace
creator: Aisha Khatri
description:
Problem: Customers running production workloads need actionable, safe recommendations to reduce inference unit costs without risking regressions. Current Optimize recommendation cards show suggestions but lack a clear, immutable audit trail of what was applied and why, diffs are noisy for batched/cached configuration, and rollback is manual and brittle.

Goal: Deliver a Console UX surface that presents batching and caching recommendations as configurable cards, shows deterministic diffs for configuration previews, and stores an immutable apply history (who/when/why) with rollback tooling. The feature must preserve safe-apply semantics used by Dedicated/Private customers and integrate with existing rollout policies and observability.

Scope:
- Recommendation cards that surface: estimated token/unit savings, expected latency impact, confidence score, and the exact config delta (quantization, batch_size, kv_cache_ttl, prefix_cache rules).
- Inline diff preview that shows before/after YAML-style config snippets and estimated cost delta for the next 30/90 days. Diffs should group changes by scope (model-route, tenant, global policy).
- Apply flow: staged apply with canary toggle, optional snapshot of previous config, and explicit confirmation with labeled risk reasons.
- Immutable apply history: audit ledger rows for every apply (user, timestamp, diff id, rollout rules, canary results, monitoring links). Ledger entries must be tamper-evident (append-only) and exportable as CSV/JSON.
- Rollback UI that proposes the minimal revert operation and simulates expected cost/latency impact.

Non-goals: automatic cross-region rebalancing, model-level kernel tuning, or changing hardware allocations. This ticket is Console UX + metadata/logging + API hooks; separate ENG tasks will implement runtime enforcement and autoscale policies.

Trade-offs considered:
- Inline simulation accuracy vs. speed: we will use heuristics + recent telemetry to project cost/latency; high-fidelity simulation is reserved for later release due to compute cost.
- Immutable ledger storage location: using existing Console DB for metadata with hash anchoring to object storage to avoid PII in long-term logs. Will revisit with Security for final approach.
- UX complexity: kept controls shallow (canary percent, duration, revert button) to avoid confusing non-platform-native users while exposing an "Advanced" drawer for power users.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards display estimated monthly token cost savings, 90-day projection, and a confidence band for latency impact.
Diff preview shows a side-by-side YAML-style before/after and an explicit list of changed keys with human-readable explanations.
Apply flow creates an immutable ledger entry containing user, timestamp, diff id, canary parameters, and a link to the runtime canary results dashboard.
Rollback flow can create a revert diff automatically and runs a dry-run simulation that updates cost/latency estimates before confirmation.
All ledger entries are exportable and visible to users with Console Auditor or Admin roles; entries cannot be edited from the UI.
Telemetry: every recommendation view, apply attempt, canary outcome, and rollback is logged to the event buffer and surfaces in the Optimize cost panel within 15 minutes.
Feature is behind a feature-flag; canary rollout to 10% of orgs and manual enable for customers in Beta program.
Design sign-off from DX with Figma mockups linked and Eng acceptance of API contracts documented in the PR.
Security review completed for log retention and PII controls (or blocked if outstanding).
